rationale: Positives: The agent authenticated the user via email and checked order details before acting. Negatives (policy-relevant): 1) The agent did not clearly restate the exact changes and obtain explicit confirmation before performing order-changing writes (returns). The user’s message indicated intent, but the policy requires the agent to state the exact change and get explicit confirmation; the agent proceeded directly to returns without a confirmation step. 2) The user’s broader intent was to refund each order to the opposite order’s payment method; the agent followed the literal mapping the user typed but failed to clarify this nuance, leading to an outcome the user rejected—proper confirmation would have prevented this. 3) The agent asserted that the refund method cannot be changed after submission without tool-based evidence or stated policy support, which risks being an unsupported claim. Given these issues, the interaction does not meet the pass bar for confirmation and correct execution aligned with the user’s intent.
